# Baseline: settings fields that are defined but registered in no sub-tab.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# A sub-tabbed settings section renders and saves ONLY the keys named in
# `get_subtab_groups()`: `render()` iterates the active group's `fields`, and
# `sanitize_with_subtabs()` whitelists input to the same list. A field declared
# in `get_fields()` but absent from every group therefore renders nowhere and is
# dropped on save, silently — the two methods are individually well-formed, so
# neither PHPCS nor a code review reliably catches it.
#
# `.github/scripts/check-settings-field-registration.php` fails when it finds a
# field in that position. This file is the BASELINE: the entries below predate
# the gate. They are recorded, not approved. Each one needs one of two outcomes:
#
#   1. Register it in the sub-tab where it belongs, then DELETE its line here.
#   2. Confirm it is written only programmatically (an integration, a migration,
#      an internal flag) and keep it listed.
#
# The gate fails on a STALE entry — a listed field that is now registered — so
# this file cannot rot, and fixing a field forces the line's removal.
#
# Format:  <repo-relative-path>:<field-key>
# Lines starting with '#' and trailing ' # ...' comments are ignored.
#
# Notable clusters as recorded (39 entries):
#   - authentication.php  3 x pseudo-fields (2 `heading`, 1 `html`) that no
#                   group references, so they render nowhere. Same registration
#                   work as the Security headings, which are now fixed.
#   - tools.php     credential and feature-flag fields with no UI group. Some
#                   are almost certainly written by integrations rather than the
#                   admin form; each needs confirmation before it is either
#                   registered or kept listed.
#
# (Section table and counts: run the script.)
